prompts.title: Copilot Adoption Dashboard
prompts.summary: Build a static HTML dashboard of Copilot adoption trends, usage patterns and organisational breakdowns.
prompts.quick_prompt:
Help me create a self-contained static HTML dashboard for people analytics and IT leaders that summarizes Copilot adoption trends and group differences from a Viva Insights person query export.
Start by loading the actual CSV and printing the row count, column names, data types, date range, and number of unique people, then map the real metric and HR columns from what is present.
Do not assume exact field names, and ask me to confirm the primary activity metric or any missing HR columns if the mapping is ambiguous.
Prefer Copilot Enabled User or Total Copilot enabled days for licensing. Under the documented native licensed-only M365 Copilot rules, null means unlicensed and zero activity means licensed but inactive. Without explicit licence fields, use a verified metric with those semantics. Do not apply this rule to unlicensed Copilot Chat or Consumption credits.
Confirm configured weekly grouping and metric windows. Date gaps do not establish cadence. Within a supplied complete query's configured scope, absent activity rows contribute zero. Failed joins, unavailable sources, out-of-scope periods and known coverage failures remain unresolved.
Build weekly adoption metrics using distinct people per week, then add the most useful group views from the available HR attributes.
The output must be a single self-contained static HTML file with inline assets and no server or external dependencies.
Suppress any group with fewer than 10 distinct people, or the stricter organisational minimum, and withhold breakdowns that could reveal suppressed cells. Do not publish individual rankings. Note skipped charts or missing segments.
At the end, list any assumptions you made about metric selection, licensing logic, or field mappings.

prompts.title: Copilot Adoption Executive Summary
prompts.summary: Summarise Copilot adoption metrics, trends and recommended actions in a memo for senior leadership.
prompts.quick_prompt:
Help me produce a concise executive summary memo for senior leaders that explains Copilot adoption progress, risks, and recommended next actions from a Viva Insights person query export.
Start by loading the real CSV and printing row count, column names, data types, date range, and unique people so you can map the actual Copilot and HR fields.
Adapt the column names dynamically rather than assuming the defaults, and ask me for the file path, preferred output format, or any ambiguous field mapping before you proceed.
Prefer Copilot Enabled User or Total Copilot enabled days per person-week. Native licensed-only M365 Copilot nulls mean unlicensed and zero activity means licensed but inactive. A verified metric with those semantics is a valid fallback without explicit licence fields. Keep failed joins and genuinely unresolved licence status separate.
Read configured grouping, week start and metric windows. Date spacing is only a diagnostic. In a supplied complete query's configured scope, absent activity rows contribute zero. Unavailable sources, out-of-scope periods and known coverage failures remain unresolved.
Calculate every reported number directly from the data, with distinct-person denominators and an explicit person versus person-week estimand.
Compare recent adoption and usage trends using the amount of history actually available, and call out when the dataset is too short for the preferred comparison window.
Keep the tone balanced and executive-friendly, include specific numbers in findings and recommendations, and avoid unsupported claims.
Suppress groups below max(the organisational requirement, 5 distinct people), including complementary cells and embedded data. Use floor 10 if this memo is part of a dashboard or joined-query workflow. Never publish individual rankings.
End by listing any assumptions you made about activity metrics, comparison windows, or segment mappings.

prompts.title: Copilot Adoption ROI Estimation
prompts.summary: Build an assumption-based Copilot value scenario from verified activity or assisted-time metrics and licence costs. Assisted time is not measured time saved or realised ROI.
prompts.quick_prompt:
Help me build an ROI summary report for finance and IT leaders that estimates the value of Copilot usage from a Viva Insights person query export.
Start by loading the actual CSV and printing row count, column names, data types, date range, and unique people so you can identify the real Copilot and collaboration fields.
Adapt to the column names that are present, and ask me for the file path, hourly rate, license cost, or any ambiguous metric mapping instead of guessing.
Prefer Copilot Enabled User or Total Copilot enabled days per person-week. Native licensed-only M365 Copilot nulls mean unlicensed and zero activity means licensed but inactive. A verified metric with those semantics is a valid fallback without explicit fields. Omit licence-dependent estimates only if licensing remains genuinely unresolved.
Read configured cadence and measurement windows, not date spacing. Within a supplied complete query's configured scope, absent activity rows contribute zero. Failed joins, unavailable sources, out-of-scope periods and known coverage failures remain unresolved.
Use a recent multi-week average, distinct-person denominators and an explicit person versus person-week estimand. Assisted hours are not measured time saved: ask me to approve a realisation factor and any proxy conversion before estimating potential value, then make the break-even threshold explicit.
Include a sensitivity analysis under multiple hourly-rate and adoption scenarios, and be explicit that any licensed versus unlicensed comparison is observational and does not prove causation.
Report negative or uncertain value scenarios honestly. Suppress groups below max(the organisational requirement, 5 distinct people), using floor 10 for dashboard/joined outputs. Protect complementary cells and embedded data; never publish individual rankings.
Finish by listing every assumption you had to make about value realization, proxies, and segment definitions.

prompts.title: Copilot Adoption Segmentation and Churn
prompts.summary: Classify Copilot users by usage intensity, track movement between segments and quantify churn. Churn measures disengagement after initial adoption.
prompts.quick_prompt:
Help me create a segmentation and churn analysis for Copilot usage that classifies licensed users, tracks movement between segments over time, and highlights at-risk groups.
Start by loading the actual CSV and printing row count, column names, data types, date range, and unique people so you can map the real activity and HR fields.
Do not assume exact column names, and ask me for the file path, the main activity metric, or any unclear field mapping before you continue.
Prefer Copilot Enabled User or Total Copilot enabled days to establish licensing. For native licensed-only M365 Copilot metrics, null means unlicensed and zero activity means licensed but inactive. A verified metric with these semantics is a valid fallback without explicit licence fields.
Use `identify_usage_segments()` (vivainsights) to compute the five weekly usage segments. If it is unavailable, clearly label any alternative segmentation and print its thresholds.
Include both week-level segment trends and a stable user segment for group breakdowns, then build a week-to-week transition matrix only for users present in consecutive weeks.
Independently of the rolling segments, define weekly activity from the observed action count. Churn means at least two consecutive active weeks followed by at least two consecutive inactive weeks; date it to the first inactive week once the second confirms it.
Identify currently at-risk users separately: they have one inactive week immediately after at least two active weeks and have not yet met the churn definition. Do not treat unknown or unlicensed weeks as inactive.
Flag if the time span is too short for reliable churn analysis.
Suppress below max(the organisational requirement, 5 distinct people), using floor 10 for dashboard/joined outputs. Protect complementary cells and embedded data, and never publish individual rankings.
Read configured weekly grouping and measurement windows, not date spacing. Within a supplied complete query's configured scope, absent activity rows contribute zero. Failed joins, out-of-scope periods and known coverage failures remain unresolved. Keep unlicensed weeks in the calendar so they break streaks and rolling eligibility windows.
End by listing any assumptions you made about thresholds, churn rules, or field mappings.

prompts.title: Executive PowerPoint Deck: Copilot Adoption
prompts.summary: Create a 10-15 slide PowerPoint deck (.pptx) with editable native charts covering Copilot adoption trends, organisational breakdowns and recommendations.
prompts.quick_prompt:
Help me generate an exec-ready PowerPoint deck that summarizes Copilot adoption for senior leaders from a Viva Insights person query export.
Start by loading the actual CSV and printing row count, column names, data types, date range, and unique people so you can map the real Copilot and HR fields before building slides.
Adapt field names dynamically, use the installed toolchain that best supports native PowerPoint charts, and ask me for the file path, template path, or any ambiguous metric mapping before you proceed.
Prefer Copilot Enabled User or Total Copilot enabled days for licensing. Native licensed-only M365 Copilot nulls mean unlicensed and zero activity means licensed but inactive. Use a verified metric with those semantics as a fallback without explicit fields. Omit rates only when licence status or licensed activity is genuinely unresolved.
Read configured cadence and measurement windows, not date spacing. In a supplied complete query's configured scope, absent activity rows contribute zero. Failed joins, out-of-scope periods and known coverage failures remain unresolved.
Create the deck directly as a .pptx file with native editable chart objects wherever the library supports them, and avoid HTML to PowerPoint conversion pipelines.
If a needed chart type cannot be created natively, simplify it to a supported native chart where possible and clearly note any remaining slide that must fall back to an image.
Use distinct-person denominators and state whether summaries weight people or person-weeks. Suppress groups below max(the organisational requirement, 5 distinct people), using floor 10 in dashboard/joined workflows. Protect complementary cells and embedded chart data; never publish individual rankings. Skip unavailable slides.
Use commentary-led slide titles and keep each number traceable to a local evidence ledger with dates, units, aggregation, bases and denominator. Related charts or tables can share a slide if labels and caveats remain readable.
For an existing user-edited deck, save a rollback, preserve unrelated content and verify the source has not changed before replacement. Remove only comments whose requested edits have been verified.
Verify numbers, embedded chart data, privacy and actual rendering separately. Report unavailable visual checks honestly.
Finish by listing any assumptions you made about chart support, metric mappings, or optional slide substitutions.

prompts.title: Copilot Causal Toolkit: Run and Interpret
prompts.summary: Help users run a causal inference analysis using the Copilot Causal Toolkit with their own data, and then interpret the results in a non-technical, business-ready format. This page contains two prompts:
prompts.quick_prompt:
Help me use the Copilot Causal Toolkit end to end by first configuring and running the right notebook for my data, then interpreting the outputs for a business audience.
Start by loading the actual CSV and printing row count, column names, data types, date range, and unique people so you can determine whether it is a Person Query or Super Users Report and map the real fields.
Do not assume exact paths or variables, and ask me for the CSV location, toolkit location, and business question if any of those are missing or ambiguous.
Keep the required two-part flow from this card, which means run and validate the analysis first, then interpret the generated outputs in a separate pass.
Do not change the treatment variable from Total_Copilot_actions_taken, do not edit shared helper modules, and warn me if the dataset is shorter than about 12 weeks.
When choosing or configuring the notebook, adapt subgroup, collaboration, and outcome variables to the columns that actually exist in my data.
Before fitting, verify the notebook's actual grain, exposure/outcome windows, pre-exposure controls, overlap and identifying assumptions. DML is not itself an identifying design. If unresolved, return readiness or an agreed association rather than a causal claim; do not run every estimator.
Prefer Copilot Enabled User or Total Copilot enabled days for licensing. Native licensed-only M365 Copilot nulls mean unlicensed and zero activity means licensed but inactive. A verified metric with these semantics is a valid fallback. Read configured cadence, not date spacing. Absent in-scope activity contributes zero, while failed joins and known coverage failures remain unresolved. Check unlicensed Copilot Chat separately before assigning causal controls.
Publish only groups meeting max(the organisational requirement, 10 distinct people), protect complementary cells and embedded data, and never publish individual rankings.
When interpreting results, explain the ATE direction in business terms, include the sensitivity analysis, and avoid overstating causation or borderline significance.
Finish each phase by listing any assumptions you made about notebook choice, variable mappings, or output interpretation.

and embedded data, protect complementary cells and never publish individual rankings.
Read configured grouping and measurement windows, not date spacing. Within a supplied
complete query's configured scope, absent activity contributes zero. Null credit
cells, failed joins, unavailable sources, out-of-scope periods and known coverage

prompts.title: Purview Audit Log Parsing
prompts.summary: Parse and clean raw Microsoft Purview audit log exports into a flat, analysis-ready dataset. This is a data engineering prompt that prepares audit log data for downstream analytics (such as the Agent Usage Analysis prompt).
prompts.quick_prompt:
Help me parse a raw Microsoft Purview audit log export into a clean flat dataset and data dictionary that are ready for downstream analysis.
Start by loading the actual file and printing row count, column names, data types, date range if available, and sample records so you can inspect the real schema before assuming any mappings.
Do not assume exact Purview or AuditData field names, and ask me for the file path or any known Copilot operation names if the mapping or filter logic is unclear.
Parse AuditData defensively with error handling, count malformed rows, and adapt extracted columns to the structures actually present in the data.
Flatten nested JSON only one level deep, keep deeper structures as JSON strings, standardize final names to snake_case, and avoid exposing raw UserIds in printed output.
If the file is large, process it in chunks, then produce both a full cleaned output and a Copilot-focused output when the filter finds relevant events.
Also generate a data dictionary that records source, type, null rate, and examples for each final column so downstream users can understand the schema.
End by listing any assumptions you made about field mappings, event classification, or anonymization.

prompts.title: Purview Agent Usage Analysis
prompts.summary: Analyse Copilot agent and extension usage from Microsoft Purview audit logs, including which features and agents are used and how group-level usage changes over time.
prompts.quick_prompt:
Help me produce an exploratory report on Copilot agent and extension usage from Microsoft Purview audit logs for program, security, and analytics stakeholders.
Start by loading the actual file and printing row count, column names, data types, date range, and sample records so you can inspect the real schema before analyzing anything.
Do not assume exact Purview field names, and ask me for the file path or confirmation of the user, timestamp, operation, workload, or AuditData fields if the mapping is ambiguous.
Use a broad first-pass filter for Copilot-related operations and workloads, show what matched, and refine the logic based on the values actually present in the data.
If AuditData exists, inspect it carefully before extracting agent or extension details, and skip that section with a clear note if those fields are unavailable.
Use static charts in a standalone HTML or notebook output, protect privacy by avoiding raw email addresses or other direct identifiers in printed output, and sample only for exploration if the dataset is very large.
Call out system-generated events, duplicates, or other schema quirks that could distort the analysis.
End by listing any assumptions you made about field mappings, Copilot filters, or agent identification.
